question: Why is password sign in impossible on production?

items.text: **AC-10**: Password sign in is impossible on production, in both places it is guarded: the sign in page does not render and the Server Action refuses to run. The enabling variable is absent there, both guards fail closed, and neither depends any longer on how a build labels `NODE_ENV`.
Auth and per user isolation

**Dev password sign in**: enabled by an explicit variable that defaults to false, set only on the Vercel Preview environment and locally. Production never carries it. Feature 7 deletes the whole feature folder.

**Already created, so record and confirm rather than create.** Both Supabase projects exist, development and production, each with the Data API set not to expose new tables. Confirm both are in `us-east-1`, then record, for each: project URL, publishable key, secret key, project ref, database password and connection string. Satisfies **AC-2**.
The development password sign in stays until feature 7 deletes it; the mint does not depend on it.

**Session mint**: a development only helper under `test/helpers/` that uses the secret client (binding rule 1, caller 1) to generate an admin magiclink for a fixture user and exchanges it with `verifyOtp` through the request scoped client into an in memory cookie jar. Guarded by `DEV_SESSION_ENABLED` (default false, fails closed). Programmatic only, no HTTP route. It does not depend on the development password sign in that feature 7 deletes.
The mint does not depend on the development password sign in from feature 1, which feature 7 deletes.
This spec builds the real sign in: OAuth through Google and GitHub, on Supabase Auth, with no password anywhere.
The development only password sign in from feature 1 is deleted along with the browser client that was only ever reserved for this feature
Email and password sign up as an alternative for people without a Google or GitHub account, password reset, session expiry handling, and an account settings screen.
**Done when:** a user can sign up and reset a password by email,
and the development only password sign in from feature 1 is deleted, not merely blocked.

**Feature 14 owns revisiting `addWorkExperience`'s duplicate submission gap**, recorded as an accepted tradeoff in `## Consequences` on 2026 09 02. Scoring is the first thing that reads work history without a person looking at it, so feature 14 is the one that can say whether duplicates need to be impossible rather than merely visible.
The production Supabase project will sit empty until feature 7 ships a way to sign in. That is expected, not a fault, though it is also the reason it will pause.

**Both hosted projects will pause, and production is the more exposed of the two.** Supabase's free plan pauses a project that has not had sufficient database activity over the previous week, and their guidance is that this means roughly a few user requests a day across that week. That is a daily bar, not a weekly one, so a burst of activity on merge day does not clear it. Production is worse off than development here: nothing touches the production database at all until feature 7 ships a way to sign in, so it will pause while being perfectly healthy. Development is exposed too whenever a few days pass with no previews.
Auth/permission: a POST to the sign in action on production is refused because `DEV_SESSION_ENABLED` is absent, verifies **AC-10**

No sign in control on the page is a link. The two provider controls render as labels carrying the `Chip` status variant, beside a line saying accounts open with feature 7. The header's "Sign in" is an in page anchor to that band and is a working link at every width. This criterion is deliberately environment independent: it holds on production, preview and locally alike, because the page never links to `/sign-in` at all.

**AC-7**: both provider controls become real `<form action={...}>` submits. What survives untouched: **AC-17**, the inert apply control, and with it this spec's one rule with no exceptions, that nothing which cannot work is a link.

**AC-16**: The entry page's two provider controls are real submits. `COPY-1` and both `Chip state="status"` labels are gone. Spec 0006 **AC-17**, the inert apply control, is untouched and its half of the "no dead controls" test still runs.
spec 0006 **AC-7** is superseded;

Replace the `NODE_ENV` guard with the validated `DEV_SESSION_ENABLED` check, failing closed, in **both** places it lives: `src/features/dev-session/actions.ts` and the page guard in `src/app/(marketing)/sign-in/page.tsx`. Satisfies **AC-10**.

**AC-13**: `DEV_SESSION_ENABLED` survives with exactly one remaining job, guarding the test mint in `test/helpers/admin.ts`. It is no longer set on Vercel Preview, `src/env.ts`'s comment about it says so, and spec 0002's configuration table matches.
**AC-2**: A push to any branch other than `main` produces a preview deployment that reads the development Supabase project. No preview ever holds credentials for the production project.
until feature 7 deletes it

This tree listed a fourth file, `lib/supabase/browser.ts`, "publishable key client", reserved for the OAuth handshake in feature 7. Feature 7 does that handshake entirely on the server, so the browser client never gained a caller and is deleted rather than left as a module whose doc comment claims a purpose it no longer has.
Layer a hard refusal on `NEXT_PUBLIC_VERCEL_ENV === "production"` on top of the `DEV_SESSION_ENABLED` guard, **in the mint only**.
`automated` No dead controls: no apply control renders as an anchor, verifies **AC-17**.
The consent screen can finally name JobHunt, closing the finding spec 0007 recorded on 2026-08-30.

Thicken: GitHub with the `user:email` scope, sign out rebuilt in `src/features/auth/` with its span and failure path, then the deletions (`src/features/dev-session/`, `src/lib/supabase/browser.ts`) and the span registry, satisfies AC-1, AC-11, AC-12, AC-13, AC-17 · done 2026-08-30.
Build the sign in controls as non linking labels with the `Chip` status variant, carrying `COPY-1`, in both the hero and the band, and wire the header's anchor to the band, satisfies **AC-7**.

**`COPY-1`, the sign in line** (**AC-7**), shown beside the two provider controls in both the hero and the sign in band. It must say that accounts are not open yet without using an internal feature number. `Sign in isn't live yet. Coming soon with Google and GitHub.`

**AC-17**: The hero card's "Apply on the real posting" control is not a link either (`JobHuntLanding.tsx` line 259 has it as `href="#"`). It renders as `Text` with the `ExternalLinkIcon`, inside `Card.Footer`. Together with **AC-7** this gives the page one rule with no exceptions: nothing that cannot work is a link, and an example listing has nothing real to apply to.

**What does not defer**: `COPY-1` and the two status chips become false for **every** visitor the moment this ships, signed in or not, and fixing them needs no session read. Those change in this feature, per AC-16.

**AC-18**: `/` renders **zero** `<form>` elements and shows no sign in invitation anywhere on the page. `SignInControls` is rendered twice today, in `src/features/entry-page/hero-section.tsx:216` and `src/features/entry-page/sign-in-band.tsx:56`, and both are replaced by the door CTA (`COPY-4`), a plain anchor that does not prefetch. The signed out header's control changes from a `#start` jump to the door (`COPY-5`), because the band it jumped to no longer signs anyone in.

**AC-2**: Each placeholder page renders an ordinary expected state, not a failure: the sentence from its copy slot (`COPY-1` to `COPY-3`), with no `role="alert"` and no red border treatment. It does not carry the literal phrase "coming soon", nor any phrasing that will become **false** once the feature lands, which is what spec 0007 **AC-16** actually deleted from the sign in band. A sentence that truthfully says a route is not built yet is fine and is what these three are.

The hero: a `<figure>` wrapping the one elevated `Card`, the example label, `MatchBar` at 8 of 11, the chip clusters, and every dead control rendered inert rather than linked, satisfies AC-5, AC-7, AC-9, AC-17

The entry page and the record: the two provider labels become real submits with `COPY-1` and both status chips deleted, spec 0006's "no dead controls" test split so its apply half survives, and the session policy matrix read off both dashboards, satisfies AC-8, AC-15, AC-16, AC-19 · **done 2026-08-30.**

After AC-18 there are no provider controls on `/`.
satisfies AC-1, AC-11, AC-12, AC-13, AC-17
What replaces it: both provider controls become real `<form action={...}>` submits.
What survives from it is the fail closed default itself, which is now the session mint's guarantee (spec 0007 **AC-13**)
Together with **AC-7** this gives the page one rule with no exceptions
Those change in this feature, per AC-16.
which is what spec 0007 **AC-16** actually deleted from the sign in band
closing the finding spec 0007 recorded on 2026-08-30

claims.text: The original reason, from 0002/AC-10, is that password sign in was guarded in two places, the sign in page and the Server Action, and both fail closed because the enabling variable is absent on production. This item is HISTORY: it was struck through and replaced by 0007.
The design constraint says the dev password sign in is enabled by an explicit variable that defaults to false, set only on Vercel Preview and locally, and production never carries it.
The build step replaced the NODE_ENV guard with the validated DEV_SESSION_ENABLED check, failing closed, in both the action and the page guard, and it satisfies AC-10.
Later, spec 0007 deleted the development password sign in altogether and builds real sign in through OAuth with no password anywhere. The scope says it is deleted, not merely blocked.
DEV_SESSION_ENABLED now guards only the test mint, and it is no longer set on Vercel Preview. The fail closed default survives as the mint's guarantee.
